newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Mersey Docks says Q1 on track.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Mersey Docks says Q1 on track.

text.p: Mersey Docks and Harbour Co chief executive Trevor Furlong said on Friday that the ports group was on track to meet first-quarter earnings expectations.
"Business has been consistently strong right across the board," he told Reuters in an interview.
Asked how the full year forecast looked, Furlong smiled broadly and said: "All I can say is that the first quarter is right in line with our expectations."
The company's announced capital expenditure target of 48 million stg remained on track, 75 percent would be invested in revenue-generating business and 25 percent in renewing assets, he said.

The company's level of debt was not a problem, with debt to equity gearing at 29.3 percent at the end of 1996. "We have always said we are prepared to go to 50 percent but we are not anywhere near that level," he said.
Mersey Docks is moving ahead with its property development plans including an office complex and four-star hotel, but Furlong said port operations would remain the core focus.
"Property is just icing on the cake," Furlong said.
On the subject of the company's long-running labour dispute with sacked dock workers, Peter Jones, director of port operations, said it would have no impact on operations in 1997.
"If you go by the first quarter you would find it impossible to identify any cost," Jones said.
Negotiations continue and the company is now considering a proposal for a labour supply cooperative.
Despite sterling's continued strength the business has not been affected.
"With the dollar and pound so strong you would think that exporters are suffering but we find they are handling record volumes.
"We charge for the container whether it is full or empty, so you might not have the same content. The indication is that certainly westward exports are very, very strong."
Asked about possible acquisitions, Furlong said: "I don't see any on the horizon but if we see something at the right time, in the right place, at the right price, we would jump at it."
Jones added: "We have enough opportunities for internal growth that we don't need to rush out and make any acquisitions."

Furlong said that Mersey Docks continued to consider possible bids for overseas ports but that it had no immediate plans. "There are opportunities overseas but it is very important that the basis is laid down very clearly.
"But there are opportunities. We will strike at the appropriate time," he said, declining to specify in what region of the world.
